module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Legendre's conjecture

*References:*
- [Landau Problems Wikipedia Page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landau%27s_problems#Twin_prime_conjecture)
- [Legendre Conjecture Wikipedia Page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legendre%27s_conjecture)
- [Luan Alberto Ferreira, *Real exponential sums over primes and prime gaps*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.08725)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter
namespace LegendreConjecture

/--
Does there always exist at least one prime between consecutive perfect squares?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem legendre_conjecture :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ n ≥ 1, ∃ p ∈ Set.Ioo (n ^ 2) ((n + 1) ^ 2), Nat.Prime p := by
  sorry

/--
If there exists a constant `c > 0` such that
`(n + 1).nth Nat.Prime - n.nth Nat.Prime < (n.nth Nat.Prime) ^ (1 / 2 - c)` for all large `n`,
then Legendre's conjecture is asymptotically true.

Formal proof linked here provided by AlphaProof.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at "https://github.com/mzhorvath1/formal-conjectures/blob/a4568d467b4f42884b6a4bd09c40d65f92113ee7/FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/LegendreConjecture.lean#L48"]
theorem bounded_gap_legendre
    (H : ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (n + 1).nth Nat.Prime - n.nth Nat.Prime <
      (n.nth Nat.Prime : ℝ) ^ (1 / (2 : ℝ) - c)) :
    ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∃ p ∈ Set.Ioo (n ^ 2) ((n + 1) ^ 2), Nat.Prime p := by
  sorry

/--
Ferreira proved that the conjecture is true for sufficiently large n.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem legendre_conjecture.ferreira_large_n :
    ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∃ p ∈ Set.Ioo (n ^ 2) ((n + 1) ^ 2), Nat.Prime p := by
  sorry

end LegendreConjecture

status_issues.recorded: @[category research solved]; the docstring says, “Ferreira proved that the conjecture is true for sufficiently large n.”
status_issues.source_status: The standard reference sources still treat the asymptotic square-root-scale prime-gap problem as unproved. Ferreira's preprint claims the result, but this is not recorded as an established resolution.
status_issues.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_gap states that the best proven uniform gap bound has exponent 0.525, describes reducing the exponent to 0.5 as conjectural, and says “All of these remain unproved.” Eventual Legendre would already imply gaps O(√p). The cited Legendre article likewise presents only weaker unconditional results. Ferreira's arXiv page, https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.08725, records v4 (7 May 2026) as “27 pages, submitted to Annals of Mathematics”; §4 Proposition 4.6 claims asymptotic Legendre, but a claimed proof is not evidence of an accepted solution.
status_issues.suggested_change: Change the category to research open and qualify the attribution as a claimed proof, unless an accepted resolution can be supplied. The asymptotic mathematical statement itself need not change.

review.notes: Checked all three declarations. The main conjecture has the correct positive-natural domain and strict interval endpoints. Ferreira's paper claims an even stronger two-prime assertion; the file states its ordinary one-prime Legendre consequence. Lean experiments confirmed real subtraction and real exponentiation in the gap hypothesis, genuine eventual quantification over ℕ, and that Nat.nth's default zero is unreachable for primes. Boundary tests exclude n = 0, verify witnesses for n = 1 and 2, and computationally check n = 1 through 100. The cited bounded_gap_legendre proof was independently compiled in /workspace/review/cited_proof_check.lean; its axioms are exactly [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], with no sorryAx. The reviewed file was not modified.
